checks: The normalized positive mixed measure is supported on the compact convex body, so its centroid is in the body even if it is not ambient interior. Convexity on every ray from that origin gives a closed interval ending at a finite attained radius, with radius zero allowed.

Positive and negative rescaled sampled fibers decrease with the positive integer distance from zero. For each slope the integer census therefore has the exact inclusive floor of the radial length, even at integer endpoints and on lower-dimensional fibers.
On both charts the absolute fiber Jacobian is k^d. The cap inequality reverses in the reflected chart. When u=0 the central fiber is entirely retained on the boundary; neither chart includes it.

The signed base and continuous moment factors are respectively ±k and ±ks. These yield g_± with k^(d+1) and the separate central first-moment term. Bounded projection and bounded continuous coordinates give finite sums and integrals.

Consecutive power-sum differences are k^d and k^(d+1), so the interpolant has increasing slopes k. Jensen applies on any measurable set of finite positive Lebesgue measure, and a single constant radial plateau gives equality.
Verified source digest and locators. The original §1 (1)–(4) gives both charts and exact moments and (5) is the same scalar convexity consequence.

overlap.comparison: Uses the same one-sided fiber Jacobian for its particular positive projective shadow and arbitrary anchor. It neither identifies the negative chart nor accounts for the actual central boundary mass and mixed-centroid moment equations.

readability: The signs in the negative chart refer to both the reflected base and continuous coordinates. The center term remains an ordinary original fiber measure.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The two reflected slope charts give exact cap masses and both centroid moments in the original mixed measure.
